documents.title: Sertraline and hyponatraemia in older adults: nested case-control study
documents.text:
PubMed — PMID 34112200 — "Sertraline and hyponatraemia in older adults: nested case-control study"
(Age and Ageing, 2022).

Among 8,912 adults aged 65 years and older starting an SSRI, current sertraline use was associated
with hyponatraemia (adjusted odds ratio 1.63, 95% CI 1.21-2.19) within the first 8 weeks of therapy.
Sodium monitoring is advised in this age group.

documents.title: SSRI use and serum sodium in young adults: a prospective cohort
documents.text:
PubMed — PMID 33557788 — "SSRI use and serum sodium in young adults: a prospective cohort"
(Journal of Psychopharmacology, 2021).

In 2,145 adults aged 18-40 years, sertraline exposure was not associated with a clinically
significant change in serum sodium over 12 weeks (mean difference -0.4 mmol/L, 95% CI -1.1 to 0.3).
No cases of hyponatraemia were observed.
